title: The Beetle Who Rolled Home by Starlight 🪲🌌
yt_title: The Beetle Who Rolled Home by Starlight 🪲🌌
yt_description:
Everyone laughed at Dot for staring at the sky… until the moon went out. 🌑
Dung beetles really do steer by the Milky Way. In planetarium tests they rolled straight under a projected Milky Way, and with tiny caps over their eyes they got lost. (Dot is a fictional character; the science is real.)

Source: Dacke, Baird, Byrne, Scholtz & Warrant (2013), "Dung Beetles Use the Milky Way for Orientation", Current Biology 23: 298–300.

caption:
Everyone laughed at the beetle staring at the sky… until the moon went out. 🪲🌌
Dung beetles really navigate by the Milky Way, scientists proved it in a planetarium.
Could YOU find your way home with no moon?

script: Every night, Dot the dung beetle rolls a ball of poo... while staring at the sky. The other beetles laugh. Look at Dot! Rolling with his head in the stars! Gus the gecko joins in. Beetles can't read stars, kid. Your eyes are way too weak. And honestly? Gus is right. Dot can't see a single star. Then the moon vanishes. New moon. The savanna goes pitch black. The other beetles grab their balls and run... in circles. Bonk. Bonk. They crash into each other, and a thief steals a ball. Gus cackles from his rock. Nobody gets home tonight! Dot climbs on top of his ball, does a little dance, and looks up. Across the whole sky, there's a faint, fuzzy stripe of light. Dot just smiles. Follow the stripe. He rolls in a perfectly straight line. Past the thieves. Past Gus. All the way home. Silence. Gus drops his snack. Dung beetles really do this: in a planetarium, they rolled straight under a fake Milky Way, and with tiny caps over their eyes, they got lost. And tomorrow night? Dot will look up again.
